name: Malaysia
void_reason: Superseded by P.U. (A) 13/2026 education levy exemption and the January 2026 contribution boundary.
change_summary: The base law from 1 October 2025: the EPF Third Schedule Parts A, C, E and F (Parts B and D deleted by Act A1760), SOCSO and EIS on the RM6,000 ceiling, the LMTD 2026 computerised-calculation specification, HRDF, and the Employment Act 1955 as amended by Act A1651 in force 1 January 2023. R44 correction: the First Schedule RM4,000 coverage comparand uses version-declared FIRST_SCHEDULE_WAGES cash classes; commission, subsistence, overtime, bonus and unclassified adjustments do not enter it. HRD correction: exclude part-time and domestic recipients, retain mandatory levy liability without registration, and require an election for the optional 5–9 class. HRD correction: declare employer scope, registration class, Form 2 count and optional threshold-crossing year; retain compulsory and optional high rates after headcount falls, including listed Part II NGOs.

limits.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(7): no more than twelve hours of work in any one day; s.60A(9) "hours of work" is the time the employee is at the employer’s disposal, so the twelve are worked hours, breaks excluded.
Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(b)
Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(c)
Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(d): not more than 45 hours of work in one week; s.60A(3) pays the hours beyond at one and a half times the hourly rate

Employment (Limitation of Overtime Work) Regulations 1980 reg. 2 sets 104 overtime hours in any one month for Employment Act 1955 s.60A(4)(a). The first proviso to s.60A(4)(a) excludes all work on a statutory rest day, a gazetted public holiday referred to in s.60D(1), or its paid substitute under s.60D. Ordinary-day and off-day overtime count; excluded days do not consume this cap. Separate daily limits and payment entitlements still apply.

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2 and 3, as substituted by the Employment (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2022 [P.U. (A) 262], in operation 1 January 2023 — the ladder in ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) and 60D(4) does not apply to a person whose wages exceed RM4,000 a month, save for the para 2 categories, which are covered irrespective of wages; para 2(4) vessel work is outside Part XII altogether; "wages" is the s.2 definition less commissions, subsistence allowance and overtime payment. The rest break is s.60A(1)(a): an employee shall not be required to work more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; proviso (i) a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours, proviso (ii) work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours inclusive of not less than forty-five minutes in the aggregate for a meal. The weekly rest day is s.59(1): every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as determined from time to time by the employer, and where more than one is allowed the LAST is the rest day for the purposes of Part XII; s.59(1A) treats any continuous period of not less than thirty hours as a rest day for shift work. holiday_rest_precedence is SUBSTITUTE on the s.60D(1) proviso: where a gazetted public holiday falls on a rest day, or on another public holiday, the working day next following is a paid holiday in substitution. APPLIED: (a) the s.60A(1)(b)-(d) statement of normal hours — not more than eight hours in one day ("normal_day"), a spread-over of not more than ten hours ("spread_day") and not more than forty-five hours in one week ("weekly_total") — enforced as schedule limits, while every BEYOND_NORMAL band below prices the overtime it derives; Applied 2026-09-18: s.60A(1)(b) the normal day is 8 hours, or up to 9 under the proviso where the contracted week is within 45 (`normal_hours`); s.60A(1)(d) 45 hours a week is a ceiling on normal hours, the hours beyond it overtime (`weekly_normal`, read by payroll), not a wall on the roster; s.60(3)(a) rest-day work of a daily- or hourly-rated employee pays one day’s wages up to half the normal hours and two days’ beyond (`person.terms.pay_frequency`); s.59(1A) the rest day does not run during maternity, sick or hospitalisation leave (`weekly_rest_rule.suspended_by_leave`); First Schedule para 2(5): a domestic employee is outside ss.60–60F and the overtime ladder (`employment.type != "DOMESTIC"`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the s.60A(7) daily limit `daily_total` is twelve WORKED hours (s.60A(9) defines hours of work as time at the employer’s disposal), not twelve clock hours less the break. Applied 2026-09-28: s.59(1) “where an employee is allowed more than one rest day in a week the last of such rest days shall be the rest day for the purposes of this Part” (`last_rest_day_only`) — an earlier REST-coded day of the same week is not the Part XII rest day, so s.60(3) does not price it: it prices as an off day, every hour beyond its (nil) normal hours at s.60A(3)(a) 1.5×. s.2 defines a week as “a continuous period of seven days” without fixing its start; the week is taken Monday–Sunday, as every weekly measure here is.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 2: a domestic employee is outside the Order. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1) and 5(1) print a daily rate by the number of working days in a week — RM65.38 (six), RM78.46 (five), RM98.08 (four) — and RM8.72 an hour. The run compares a daily contract as the month it makes (the rate × the 26-day divisor), so `scale` restates the printed daily rate as that month over the printed monthly RM1,700; `hourly_by_region` holds an hourly rate to RM8.72 directly (the three figures are one table of the Order and move together); a monthly contract is the monthly RM1,700 (scale 1). Para 2 excludes only a domestic servant; the INTERN exclusion rests on an intern on industrial training not being employed under a contract of service.

encashment.authority: Employment Act 1955 ss.2, 60E(3A), 60I(1A)-(1B): monthly wages / 26; weekly basic / 6. Contract allowances are monthly amounts, so qualifying normal-hours allowances add their monthly amount / 26. Excluded payments do not enter the rate.; s.60I(1C) for daily/hourly rates (preceding wage period)

ordinary_rate_reference.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60I(1C): total wages in the preceding wage period over the days actually worked

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.24(8): the total deducted under s.24 in a month may not exceed 50% of the wages earned in that month — s.24(2)(d) deductions authorized by another written law (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, MTD) are deductions under the section, and s.24(2)(c)/(4)(b) advance and loan recoveries count; s.24(9)(b) excludes from the limit only “deductions from the final payment of the wages of an employee for any amount due to the employer and remaining unpaid by the employee on the termination of the employee’s contract of service” — the loan and advance recoveries; the statutory and other deductions on the final payslip stay within the half (round 5, Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023). Applied: s.24(9)(a) exempts deductions FROM the notice indemnity payable BY the employer TO the employee (NOTICE_IN_LIEU), up to that payment; it does not generally exempt an indemnity owed by the employee. NOTICE_INDEMNITY is lawful under s.24(2)(b) and outside the half only on final pay under s.24(9)(b); s.24(9)(c) permits up to a further 25% solely for APPROVED_HOUSING_LOAN with the Director General's written permission recorded in approval_reference. The extra room never increases ordinary deductions. EA s.2 wage exclusions are classified by basis_exempt_codes; customer-specific codes must be classified in the sealed settings. Settled 2026-09-23 (round 4) from the Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023: s.24(1) “No deductions shall be made by an employer from the wages of an employee otherwise than in accordance with this Act”; s.24(2) “It shall be lawful for an employer to make the following deductions: … (d) deductions authorized by any other written law”; s.24(8) “The total of any amounts deducted under this section from the wages of an employee in respect of any one month shall not exceed fifty per centum of the wages earned by that employee in that month.” A statutory deduction (EPF employee share, SOCSO, EIS, MTD/PCB) is lawful only through s.24(2)(d) — s.24(1) admits no other route — so it is deducted under this section and counts toward the half; s.24(9) exempts it nowhere. The statutory charges are never shortened: they take their room first and only the counted recoveries are dropped.

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.21(2): an employee who terminates without notice under s.13(1)-(2) or s.14(3) is paid not later than the third day after the termination

Employment Act 1955 s.20 (a contract ending under s.11(1) or by notice under s.12, from either party) and s.21(1) (the employer terminating without notice): not later than the day the contract terminates

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
lom.agc.gov.my — Laws of Malaysia (AGC): every Act and gazette order. The consolidated reprint of a principal Act is /ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act <n>.pdf (452 EPF, 4 SOCSO, 265 Employment, 53 Income Tax; text); an amending Act is a PDF at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/<id>_BI/<Act name>.pdf; a P.U.(A)/(B) order at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/<id>/PUB <n> (<year>).pdf. Use the exact PDF URL listed; the portal search is script-driven and not readable.
kwsp.gov.my — EPF. /en/employer/responsibilities/mandatory-contribution states the Part A/C/E rates, the age gates and the age-75 stop (HTML). /documents/d/guest/third_schedule_from_-1-october-2025 is the Third Schedule download link (the reader gets a shell page; the 1,203-row table is the PDF behind it). /en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees is Part F.
perkeso.gov.my — SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK. /en/rate-of-contribution.html carries the Act 4 / Act 800 tables; /images/lindung/lindung-24-jam/NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf is the 65-row table with the SKBBK column (0.2 MB, text); /en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html holds the SKBBK notice and FAQ PDF.
hasil.gov.my — LHDN MTD. /majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data/ lists the yearly "Spesifikasi Kaedah Pengiraan Berkomputer PCB <year>" PDF (/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-<year>.pdf, 1.3 MB, text): Table 1 rates, reliefs, the RM10 minimum.
lom.agc.gov.my — Employment Act 1955 reprint as at 1 August 2023 (Commissioner of Law Revision; latest amendment A1651): /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint Act 265 (Final).pdf (1.6 MB, text): ss.60, 60A, 60D, 60E, 60F, First Schedule.
jtksm.mohr.gov.my — /sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta Kerja 1955 (Akta 265).pdf is only the AGC updated text as at 1 January 2023, which states it is not an authentic text; cite the reprint instead. /ms/soalan-lazim/akta-kerja-1955-pindaan-2022 is the 2022 amendment FAQ.
gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my — the Minimum Wages Order in force, as one figure on the landing page.
hrdcorp.gov.my — HRD levy; the site sits behind a browser challenge the reader cannot pass, so note it rather than reading it.
johor.gov.my/rakyat/cuti-umum-2 — the Johor state holiday list for the year.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
1) lom.agc.gov.my: open subsid.php?type=pua, subsid.php?type=pub and principal.php?type=amendment (JS tables, newest first) plus the home page's 7-day What's New. Title search by URL (JS results, relevance order, scan every row for the year): search.php?search=<words>&kategori=iagcpuab_pua|iagcpuab_pub|iagcact_amendment|all&sorting=newest&lookup=title. Queries: 'minimum wages', 'employees provident fund', 'employees social security', 'employment insurance system', 'income tax (deduction from remuneration)', 'employment', 'holidays', 'human resources development'. Read the commencement clause, and check P.U.(B) for appointed dates of NOT YET IN FORCE Acts. Updated Acts: principal.php?type=updated. 2) LHDN: pengumuman-kenyataan-media and ketetapan-umum; PCB spec on majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data. 3) PERKESO directives-circulars. 4) KWSP highlights (browser). 5) JTKSM kenyataan-media for ad hoc state holidays; kabinet.gov.my for the yearly schedule. 6) Budget: belanjawan.mof.gov.my (October). hrdcorp.gov.my sits behind a Cloudflare challenge; do not attempt it; use PSMB Act/P.U.(A) on LOM. Discovery only: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/malaysia/individual/significant-developments — then cite the gazette or agency page.

obligations.description: Payment of wages
obligations.trigger: End of each wage period (not exceeding one month, s.18)
obligations.timing: Not later than the seventh day after the last day of the wage period; rest-day, public-holiday and overtime wages not later than the last day of the next wage period; the Director General may extend on application
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) ss.18(1), 19(1)-(3) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Deductions from wages limited to those the Act permits
obligations.trigger: Any deduction from wages
obligations.timing: At each payment: only deductions under s.24 (and s.25A payment method); advances capped by s.22
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) ss.22, 24, 25A (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Pay not less than the minimum wages rates
obligations.trigger: Every covered employee, each wage period
obligations.timing: From 1 February 2025 (employers of five or more, and MASCO professional activities) and 1 August 2025 (all others): RM1,700 a month, RM65.38/RM78.46/RM98.08 a day for a six-, five- or four-day week, RM8.72 an hour; piece-rate/commission-only pay not less than RM1,700 a month; domestic servants excluded
obligations.owner: HR and Payroll / contract and payslips

obligations.description: Overtime within the statutory ceiling
obligations.trigger: Overtime work

obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.60FA(1)-(3) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.owner: HR / notice to the nearest Labour office
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.63A (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

exit_facts.label: Left without notice
exit_facts.description: The employee ended the contract without notice under Employment Act 1955 s.13(1)-(2) or s.14(3); the final wages are then due by the third day after (s.21(2)).
exit_facts.required_when: employment.exit_reason == "RESIGNATION"

exit_facts.label: Leaving Malaysia for more than three months
exit_facts.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.83(4): the employer gives CP21 notice and withholds money payable under s.83(5).
exit_facts.required_when: employee.citizenship == "CITIZEN" && !(employment.exit_reason in ["RETIREMENT", "DEATH"])

exit_facts.label: Wages of the last twelve months
exit_facts.description: Termination and Lay-Off Benefits Regulations 1980 reg.6(2): the s.2 wages earned in the twelve completed months before termination, stated where earlier payslips in this workspace do not hold them (an employee brought over with history). Absent, the termination benefit reads the payslips.

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for misconduct
exit_facts.description: Dismissed for misconduct after due inquiry. Statutory consequences apply only where the relevant provision covers the worker; domestic service is excluded from s.14; s.57 and Part XVA have distinct grounds. For covered workers s.60E(3A) also governs untaken annual leave.
exit_facts.required_when: employment.exit_reason == "DISMISSAL"

exit_facts.label: Written termination notice given
exit_facts.description: Whether written notice was given before departure. Its giving day counts in the notice period (Employment Act s.12(4)). Without notice, the whole prospective period is unserved.
exit_facts.required_when: (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception == "NONE"

exit_facts.label: Written notice date (YYYY-MM-DD)
exit_facts.description: Actual date notice was given, within this employment and no later than the final service day. Service thresholds are assessed on this date.
exit_facts.required_when: ((employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception == "NONE") && employment.exit_facts.notice_given
exit_facts.validation_message: The written notice date requires notice to have been given and must fall within the employment through its final service day.

exit_facts.label: Final unserved notice days waived
exit_facts.description: Calendar days at the END of the remaining notice period expressly waived by the party entitled to notice. Enter 0 where no waiver exists. Record the agreement; a waiver cannot exceed the unserved period.
exit_facts.required_when: (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception == "NONE"

exit_facts.label: Party ending employment on the final service day
exit_facts.description: The party electing to end employment on this date, including cutting short an earlier notice. EMPLOYER owes the employee; EMPLOYEE may owe the employer. NEITHER is natural expiry, death or an agreed end with no unilateral termination. The original resignation/dismissal label alone does not decide this.
exit_facts.required_when: employment.exit_date != ""

exit_facts.label: Approved and filed apprenticeship contract
exit_facts.description: True only for an apprenticeship contract in a form approved by the Director General AND a copy filed with the Director General (EA s.17A). A trainee/intern label is insufficient. Sections 10–16 then do not apply; separate contractual rights still require assessment.
exit_facts.required_when: employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]

exit_facts.label: Ground permitting termination without notice indemnity
exit_facts.description: NONE for ordinary notice. OTHER_PARTY_WILFUL_BREACH: s.13(2). IMMEDIATE_DANGER: employee/dependants immediately threatened by violence/disease not undertaken under the contract, s.14(3), outside domestic service. DOMESTIC_INCONSISTENT_CONDUCT: the other party's conduct contrary to the domestic-service contract, s.57. Due-inquiry misconduct is recorded separately. HARASSMENT_DISMISSAL: employer dismissal after its inquiry proves sexual harassment, s.81C(a)(i); Part XVA also applies to domestic employees and approved apprentices. This is not a complainant departure under s.81E.
exit_facts.required_when: (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true)
exit_facts.validation_message: The notice exception does not apply to this terminating party or employment category.

exit_facts.label: Section 12(3) termination ground
exit_facts.description: The specified closure/reduction/ownership grounds and refusal of a transfer the contract does not require preserve the 4/6/8-week floor even where the written contract is shorter. Redundancy/retrenchment labels also retain that floor.
exit_facts.required_when: ((employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception == "NONE") && employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC"
exit_facts.validation_message: Section 12(3) grounds require an employer termination covered by section 12.

exit_facts.label: Notice exception or approval evidence reference
exit_facts.description: Reference to the breach/danger/inquiry or proven sexual-harassment dismissal record, domestic contract conduct, apprenticeship approval and filed copy, or the section 12(3) cause. Preserve the underlying evidence.
exit_facts.required_when: (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) || (employment.exit_facts.notice_exception != "" && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception != "NONE") || (employment.exit_facts.notice_structural_ground != "" && employment.exit_facts.notice_structural_ground != "NONE"))

name: Malaysia — 2026-06-01
void_reason: Superseded by P.U. (A) 13/2026 education levy exemption and the January 2026 contribution boundary.
change_summary: SKBBK / LINDUNG 24 Jam comes into operation on 1 June 2026: an employee-borne 0.75% contribution (Phase 1) on the SOCSO wage bands and the RM6,000 ceiling, charged in both PERKESO categories. EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB and HRDF are unchanged. R44 correction: the First Schedule RM4,000 coverage comparand uses version-declared FIRST_SCHEDULE_WAGES cash classes; commission, subsistence, overtime, bonus and unclassified adjustments do not enter it. HRD correction: exclude part-time and domestic recipients, retain mandatory levy liability without registration, and require an election for the optional 5–9 class. HRD correction: declare employer scope, registration class, Form 2 count and optional threshold-crossing year; retain compulsory and optional high rates after headcount falls, including listed Part II NGOs.

limits.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(7): no more than twelve hours of work in any one day; s.60A(9) "hours of work" is the time the employee is at the employer’s disposal, so the twelve are worked hours, breaks excluded.
Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(b)
Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(c)
Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(d): not more than 45 hours of work in one week; s.60A(3) pays the hours beyond at one and a half times the hourly rate

Employment (Limitation of Overtime Work) Regulations 1980 reg. 2 sets 104 overtime hours in any one month for Employment Act 1955 s.60A(4)(a). The first proviso to s.60A(4)(a) excludes all work on a statutory rest day, a gazetted public holiday referred to in s.60D(1), or its paid substitute under s.60D. Ordinary-day and off-day overtime count; excluded days do not consume this cap. Separate daily limits and payment entitlements still apply.

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2 and 3, as substituted by the Employment (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2022 [P.U. (A) 262], in operation 1 January 2023 — the ladder in ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) and 60D(4) does not apply to a person whose wages exceed RM4,000 a month, save for the para 2 categories, which are covered irrespective of wages; para 2(4) vessel work is outside Part XII altogether; "wages" is the s.2 definition less commissions, subsistence allowance and overtime payment. The rest break is s.60A(1)(a): an employee shall not be required to work more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; proviso (i) a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours, proviso (ii) work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours inclusive of not less than forty-five minutes in the aggregate for a meal. The weekly rest day is s.59(1): every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as determined from time to time by the employer, and where more than one is allowed the LAST is the rest day for the purposes of Part XII; s.59(1A) treats any continuous period of not less than thirty hours as a rest day for shift work. holiday_rest_precedence is SUBSTITUTE on the s.60D(1) proviso: where a gazetted public holiday falls on a rest day, or on another public holiday, the working day next following is a paid holiday in substitution. APPLIED: (a) the s.60A(1)(b)-(d) statement of normal hours — not more than eight hours in one day ("normal_day"), a spread-over of not more than ten hours ("spread_day") and not more than forty-five hours in one week ("weekly_total") — enforced as schedule limits, while every BEYOND_NORMAL band below prices the overtime it derives; Applied 2026-09-18: s.60A(1)(b) the normal day is 8 hours, or up to 9 under the proviso where the contracted week is within 45 (`normal_hours`); s.60A(1)(d) 45 hours a week is a ceiling on normal hours, the hours beyond it overtime (`weekly_normal`, read by payroll), not a wall on the roster; s.60(3)(a) rest-day work of a daily- or hourly-rated employee pays one day’s wages up to half the normal hours and two days’ beyond (`person.terms.pay_frequency`); s.59(1A) the rest day does not run during maternity, sick or hospitalisation leave (`weekly_rest_rule.suspended_by_leave`); First Schedule para 2(5): a domestic employee is outside ss.60–60F and the overtime ladder (`employment.type != "DOMESTIC"`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the s.60A(7) daily limit `daily_total` is twelve WORKED hours (s.60A(9) defines hours of work as time at the employer’s disposal), not twelve clock hours less the break. Applied 2026-09-28: s.59(1) “where an employee is allowed more than one rest day in a week the last of such rest days shall be the rest day for the purposes of this Part” (`last_rest_day_only`) — an earlier REST-coded day of the same week is not the Part XII rest day, so s.60(3) does not price it: it prices as an off day, every hour beyond its (nil) normal hours at s.60A(3)(a) 1.5×. s.2 defines a week as “a continuous period of seven days” without fixing its start; the week is taken Monday–Sunday, as every weekly measure here is.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 2: a domestic employee is outside the Order. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1) and 5(1) print a daily rate by the number of working days in a week — RM65.38 (six), RM78.46 (five), RM98.08 (four) — and RM8.72 an hour. The run compares a daily contract as the month it makes (the rate × the 26-day divisor), so `scale` restates the printed daily rate as that month over the printed monthly RM1,700; `hourly_by_region` holds an hourly rate to RM8.72 directly (the three figures are one table of the Order and move together); a monthly contract is the monthly RM1,700 (scale 1). Para 2 excludes only a domestic servant; the INTERN exclusion rests on an intern on industrial training not being employed under a contract of service.

encashment.authority: Employment Act 1955 ss.2, 60E(3A), 60I(1A)-(1B): monthly wages / 26; weekly basic / 6. Contract allowances are monthly amounts, so qualifying normal-hours allowances add their monthly amount / 26. Excluded payments do not enter the rate.; s.60I(1C) for daily/hourly rates (preceding wage period)

ordinary_rate_reference.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60I(1C): total wages in the preceding wage period over the days actually worked

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.24(8): the total deducted under s.24 in a month may not exceed 50% of the wages earned in that month — s.24(2)(d) deductions authorized by another written law (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, MTD) are deductions under the section, and s.24(2)(c)/(4)(b) advance and loan recoveries count; s.24(9)(b) excludes from the limit only “deductions from the final payment of the wages of an employee for any amount due to the employer and remaining unpaid by the employee on the termination of the employee’s contract of service” — the loan and advance recoveries; the statutory and other deductions on the final payslip stay within the half (round 5, Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023). Applied: s.24(9)(a) exempts deductions FROM the notice indemnity payable BY the employer TO the employee (NOTICE_IN_LIEU), up to that payment; it does not generally exempt an indemnity owed by the employee. NOTICE_INDEMNITY is lawful under s.24(2)(b) and outside the half only on final pay under s.24(9)(b); s.24(9)(c) permits up to a further 25% solely for APPROVED_HOUSING_LOAN with the Director General's written permission recorded in approval_reference. The extra room never increases ordinary deductions. EA s.2 wage exclusions are classified by basis_exempt_codes; customer-specific codes must be classified in the sealed settings. Settled 2026-09-23 (round 4) from the Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023: s.24(1) “No deductions shall be made by an employer from the wages of an employee otherwise than in accordance with this Act”; s.24(2) “It shall be lawful for an employer to make the following deductions: … (d) deductions authorized by any other written law”; s.24(8) “The total of any amounts deducted under this section from the wages of an employee in respect of any one month shall not exceed fifty per centum of the wages earned by that employee in that month.” A statutory deduction (EPF employee share, SOCSO, EIS, MTD/PCB) is lawful only through s.24(2)(d) — s.24(1) admits no other route — so it is deducted under this section and counts toward the half; s.24(9) exempts it nowhere. The statutory charges are never shortened: they take their room first and only the counted recoveries are dropped.

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.21(2): an employee who terminates without notice under s.13(1)-(2) or s.14(3) is paid not later than the third day after the termination

Employment Act 1955 s.20 (a contract ending under s.11(1) or by notice under s.12, from either party) and s.21(1) (the employer terminating without notice): not later than the day the contract terminates

tax_clearance.when: employment.exit_reason == "RETIREMENT" || employee.citizenship != "CITIZEN" || ("leaving_malaysia" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.leaving_malaysia == true)
tax_clearance.authority: Income Tax Act 1967 s.83(3)-(5): notice one month before a retiring employee ceases (the MTD exemption in the s.83(3) proviso does not reach a retiree) or before an employee leaves Malaysia for more than three months; money withheld until ninety days after HASiL receives it; e-SPC

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
lom.agc.gov.my — Laws of Malaysia (AGC): every Act and gazette order. The consolidated reprint of a principal Act is /ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act <n>.pdf (452 EPF, 4 SOCSO, 265 Employment, 53 Income Tax; text); an amending Act is a PDF at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/<id>_BI/<Act name>.pdf; a P.U.(A)/(B) order at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/<id>/PUB <n> (<year>).pdf. Use the exact PDF URL listed; the portal search is script-driven and not readable.
kwsp.gov.my — EPF. /en/employer/responsibilities/mandatory-contribution states the Part A/C/E rates, the age gates and the age-75 stop (HTML). /documents/d/guest/third_schedule_from_-1-october-2025 is the Third Schedule download link (the reader gets a shell page; the 1,203-row table is the PDF behind it). /en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees is Part F.
perkeso.gov.my — SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK. /en/rate-of-contribution.html carries the Act 4 / Act 800 tables; /images/lindung/lindung-24-jam/NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf is the 65-row table with the SKBBK column (0.2 MB, text); /en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html holds the SKBBK notice and FAQ PDF.
hasil.gov.my — LHDN MTD. /majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data/ lists the yearly "Spesifikasi Kaedah Pengiraan Berkomputer PCB <year>" PDF (/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-<year>.pdf, 1.3 MB, text): Table 1 rates, reliefs, the RM10 minimum.
lom.agc.gov.my — Employment Act 1955 reprint as at 1 August 2023 (Commissioner of Law Revision; latest amendment A1651): /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint Act 265 (Final).pdf (1.6 MB, text): ss.60, 60A, 60D, 60E, 60F, First Schedule.
jtksm.mohr.gov.my — /sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta Kerja 1955 (Akta 265).pdf is only the AGC updated text as at 1 January 2023, which states it is not an authentic text; cite the reprint instead. /ms/soalan-lazim/akta-kerja-1955-pindaan-2022 is the 2022 amendment FAQ.
gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my — the Minimum Wages Order in force, as one figure on the landing page.
hrdcorp.gov.my — HRD levy; the site sits behind a browser challenge the reader cannot pass, so note it rather than reading it.
johor.gov.my/rakyat/cuti-umum-2 — the Johor state holiday list for the year.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
1) lom.agc.gov.my: open subsid.php?type=pua, subsid.php?type=pub and principal.php?type=amendment (JS tables, newest first) plus the home page's 7-day What's New. Title search by URL (JS results, relevance order, scan every row for the year): search.php?search=<words>&kategori=iagcpuab_pua|iagcpuab_pub|iagcact_amendment|all&sorting=newest&lookup=title. Queries: 'minimum wages', 'employees provident fund', 'employees social security', 'employment insurance system', 'income tax (deduction from remuneration)', 'employment', 'holidays', 'human resources development'. Read the commencement clause, and check P.U.(B) for appointed dates of NOT YET IN FORCE Acts. Updated Acts: principal.php?type=updated. 2) LHDN: pengumuman-kenyataan-media and ketetapan-umum; PCB spec on majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data. 3) PERKESO directives-circulars. 4) KWSP highlights (browser). 5) JTKSM kenyataan-media for ad hoc state holidays; kabinet.gov.my for the yearly schedule. 6) Budget: belanjawan.mof.gov.my (October). hrdcorp.gov.my sits behind a Cloudflare challenge; do not attempt it; use PSMB Act/P.U.(A) on LOM. Discovery only: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/malaysia/individual/significant-developments — then cite the gazette or agency page.

obligations.description: Written contract of service with a termination clause

obligations.description: Separate statement of wages for each wage period (reg. 5(c) particulars)

obligations.description: Register of employees with personal details, terms and per-period wages

obligations.timing: Wage-period particulars brought up to date not later than the 3rd day after the end of each wage period; every particular kept available for inspection for not less than six years; kept at the place of employment and open to the employee twice a wage period
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.61(1)-(2) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf); Employment Regulations 1957 [P.U.(A) 333/1983] regs. 5-7 (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-03/1.%20EMPLOYMENT%20REGULATIONS%201957_0.pdf)

obligations.description: Payment of wages
obligations.trigger: End of each wage period (not exceeding one month, s.18)
obligations.timing: Not later than the seventh day after the last day of the wage period; rest-day, public-holiday and overtime wages not later than the last day of the next wage period; the Director General may extend on application
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) ss.18(1), 19(1)-(3) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Deductions from wages limited to those the Act permits
obligations.trigger: Any deduction from wages
obligations.timing: At each payment: only deductions under s.24 (and s.25A payment method); advances capped by s.22
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) ss.22, 24, 25A (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Pay not less than the minimum wages rates
obligations.trigger: Every covered employee, each wage period
obligations.timing: From 1 February 2025 (employers of five or more, and MASCO professional activities) and 1 August 2025 (all others): RM1,700 a month, RM65.38/RM78.46/RM98.08 a day for a six-, five- or four-day week, RM8.72 an hour; piece-rate/commission-only pay not less than RM1,700 a month; domestic servants excluded
obligations.owner: HR and Payroll / contract and payslips
obligations.authority: Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 2, 3 and 5 (https://gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/PUA%20376.pdf); National Wages Consultative Council Act 2011 (Act 732) s.23

obligations.description: Overtime within the statutory ceiling
obligations.trigger: Overtime work
obligations.timing: Not more than 104 hours of overtime in any one month without the Director General’s written permission; normal hours not more than 8 a day (9 under the proviso) and 45 a week; not more than 12 hours of work a day
obligations.authority: Employment (Limitation of Overtime Work) Regulations 1980 reg. 2 (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-03/7.%20EMPLOYMENT%20%28LIMITATION%20OF%20OVERTIME%20WORK%29%20REGULATIONS%201980_0.pdf); Employment Act 1955 s.60A(4)(a) and provisos, s.60A(7)

obligations.description: Decision on a flexible working arrangement application
obligations.trigger: A written application under s.60P
obligations.timing: Approve or refuse in writing within sixty days of receipt, stating the ground of any refusal
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) ss.60P-60Q (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Paternity leave notice and eligibility evidence
obligations.trigger: Application under s.60FA by a married male employee with twelve months’ service
obligations.timing: Employee notifies at least thirty days before the expected confinement or as early as possible after it; seven consecutive days per confinement, up to five confinements
obligations.owner: HR / notice, marriage and confinement evidence
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.60FA(1)-(3) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Notice of an undertaking or establishment to the Labour Department
obligations.trigger: Commencing operation, taking over, or changing the name or location of an establishment employing employees
obligations.timing: Within ninety days of commencing operation, taking over or the change: registered name, address, nature of business, person in charge and employee categories and numbers
obligations.owner: HR / notice to the nearest Labour office
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.63A (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Director General’s approval to employ a foreign employee
obligations.trigger: Employing a foreign employee (not a permanent resident, s.60O)
obligations.timing: Prior approval before employment; particulars of the foreign employee furnished within fourteen days of the date of employment
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) ss.60K(1)-(3), 60O (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Notice to the Director General of a foreign employee’s termination
obligations.trigger: Termination by the employer, expiry of the employment pass or repatriation/deportation; or the employee’s own termination or absconding
obligations.timing: Within thirty days of the termination (employer, pass expiry, repatriation); within fourteen days of the employee’s termination or absence (absconding)
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.60KA(1)-(2) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Annual foreign worker levy for each Visit Pass (Temporary Employment) holder
obligations.trigger: Issue and each renewal of a foreign worker’s VP(TE)
obligations.timing: Paid by the employer to the Director General of Immigration when the Visit Pass (Temporary Employment) is issued and at each extension (extension may be applied for 3 months before expiry): RM1,850 a year for manufacturing, construction and services, RM640 for plantation and agriculture (Peninsular Malaysia). Borne by the employer; not a deduction EA 1955 s.24 permits from wages.
obligations.authority: Immigration Department of Malaysia, Foreign Worker service page (levy table), https://www.imi.gov.my/index.php/en/main-services/foreign-worker/; levy imposed under the Fees Act 1951 (Act 209); Employment Act 1955 s.24 (lawful deductions).

obligations.description: Foreign employees retrenched before local employees in a similar capacity
obligations.trigger: Redundancy necessitating retrenchment
obligations.timing: Before terminating any local employee, terminate all foreign employees in a similar capacity; no local terminated in order to employ a foreigner
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) ss.60M-60N (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Retrenchment notification (Borang PK with Lampiran 1)
obligations.trigger: Retrenchment, voluntary separation scheme, temporary lay-off or pay cut; not required for disciplinary dismissal
obligations.timing: At least thirty days before the action takes effect, to the nearest Labour Department office
obligations.authority: Pemberitahuan Pemberhentian Pekerja 2004 (Borang PK) [P.U.(B) 430/2004] under Employment Act 1955 s.63; JTKSM, Employees’ Retrenchment FAQ (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/en/frequently-asked-questions/employees-retrenchment)

obligations.description: Statutory notice on a redundancy-type termination
obligations.trigger: Termination attributable to closure, relocation, diminished requirement, refused transfer or change of ownership

obligations.owner: HR and Payroll / notice letter or indemnity payment
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) ss.12(2)-(4), 13(1) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Final wages on termination

obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) ss.20-21 (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf)

obligations.description: Termination or lay-off benefits payment with a written statement of its calculation

obligations.authority: Employment (Termination and Lay-Off Benefits) Regulations 1980 regs. 3-6, 11, 12 (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-03/8.%20EMPLOYMENT%20(TERMINATION%20&%20LAY%20OFF%20BENEFITS)%20REGULATIONS%201980_0.pdf)

exit_facts.label: Left without notice
exit_facts.description: The employee ended the contract without notice under Employment Act 1955 s.13(1)-(2) or s.14(3); the final wages are then due by the third day after (s.21(2)).
exit_facts.required_when: employment.exit_reason == "RESIGNATION"

exit_facts.label: Leaving Malaysia for more than three months
exit_facts.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.83(4): the employer gives CP21 notice and withholds money payable under s.83(5).
exit_facts.required_when: employee.citizenship == "CITIZEN" && !(employment.exit_reason in ["RETIREMENT", "DEATH"])

exit_facts.label: Wages of the last twelve months
exit_facts.description: Termination and Lay-Off Benefits Regulations 1980 reg.6(2): the s.2 wages earned in the twelve completed months before termination, stated where earlier payslips in this workspace do not hold them (an employee brought over with history). Absent, the termination benefit reads the payslips.

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for misconduct
exit_facts.description: Dismissed for misconduct after due inquiry. Statutory consequences apply only where the relevant provision covers the worker; domestic service is excluded from s.14; s.57 and Part XVA have distinct grounds. For covered workers s.60E(3A) also governs untaken annual leave.
exit_facts.required_when: employment.exit_reason == "DISMISSAL"

exit_facts.label: Written termination notice given
exit_facts.description: Whether written notice was given before departure. Its giving day counts in the notice period (Employment Act s.12(4)). Without notice, the whole prospective period is unserved.
exit_facts.required_when: (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception == "NONE"

exit_facts.label: Written notice date (YYYY-MM-DD)
exit_facts.description: Actual date notice was given, within this employment and no later than the final service day. Service thresholds are assessed on this date.
exit_facts.required_when: ((employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception == "NONE") && employment.exit_facts.notice_given
exit_facts.validation_message: The written notice date requires notice to have been given and must fall within the employment through its final service day.

exit_facts.label: Final unserved notice days waived
exit_facts.description: Calendar days at the END of the remaining notice period expressly waived by the party entitled to notice. Enter 0 where no waiver exists. Record the agreement; a waiver cannot exceed the unserved period.
exit_facts.required_when: (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception == "NONE"

exit_facts.label: Party ending employment on the final service day
exit_facts.description: The party electing to end employment on this date, including cutting short an earlier notice. EMPLOYER owes the employee; EMPLOYEE may owe the employer. NEITHER is natural expiry, death or an agreed end with no unilateral termination. The original resignation/dismissal label alone does not decide this.
exit_facts.required_when: employment.exit_date != ""

exit_facts.label: Approved and filed apprenticeship contract
exit_facts.description: True only for an apprenticeship contract in a form approved by the Director General AND a copy filed with the Director General (EA s.17A). A trainee/intern label is insufficient. Sections 10–16 then do not apply; separate contractual rights still require assessment.
exit_facts.required_when: employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]

exit_facts.label: Ground permitting termination without notice indemnity
exit_facts.description: NONE for ordinary notice. OTHER_PARTY_WILFUL_BREACH: s.13(2). IMMEDIATE_DANGER: employee/dependants immediately threatened by violence/disease not undertaken under the contract, s.14(3), outside domestic service. DOMESTIC_INCONSISTENT_CONDUCT: the other party's conduct contrary to the domestic-service contract, s.57. Due-inquiry misconduct is recorded separately. HARASSMENT_DISMISSAL: employer dismissal after its inquiry proves sexual harassment, s.81C(a)(i); Part XVA also applies to domestic employees and approved apprentices. This is not a complainant departure under s.81E.
exit_facts.required_when: (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true)
exit_facts.validation_message: The notice exception does not apply to this terminating party or employment category.

exit_facts.label: Section 12(3) termination ground
exit_facts.description: The specified closure/reduction/ownership grounds and refusal of a transfer the contract does not require preserve the 4/6/8-week floor even where the written contract is shorter. Redundancy/retrenchment labels also retain that floor.
exit_facts.required_when: ((employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (!employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || employment.type == "DOMESTIC") && !(employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception == "NONE") && employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC"
exit_facts.validation_message: Section 12(3) grounds require an employer termination covered by section 12.

exit_facts.label: Notice exception or approval evidence reference
exit_facts.description: Reference to the breach/danger/inquiry or proven sexual-harassment dismissal record, domestic contract conduct, apprenticeship approval and filed copy, or the section 12(3) cause. Preserve the underlying evidence.
exit_facts.required_when: (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party in ["EMPLOYER", "EMPLOYEE"]) && (employment.exit_facts.notice_approved_apprenticeship || (employment.exit_facts.notice_termination_party == "EMPLOYER" && employment.type != "DOMESTIC" && "misconduct_dismissal" in employment.exit_fact_keys && employment.exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal == true) || (employment.exit_facts.notice_exception != "" && employment.exit_facts.notice_exception != "NONE") || (employment.exit_facts.notice_structural_ground != "" && employment.exit_facts.notice_structural_ground != "NONE"))

name: Malaysia — 2026-07-08
void_reason: Superseded by P.U. (A) 13/2026 education levy exemption and the January 2026 contribution boundary.
change_summary: The Cabinet makes SKBBK voluntary for Malaysian citizens and permanent residents with immediate effect on 8 July 2026 (KESUMA confirmed on 9 July; the opt-out window ran 13 July to 31 August). Foreign workers remain mandatory; a local’s Release of Liability is a per-employment NOT_REGISTERED fact. R44 correction: the First Schedule RM4,000 coverage comparand uses version-declared FIRST_SCHEDULE_WAGES cash classes; commission, subsistence, overtime, bonus and unclassified adjustments do not enter it. HRD correction: exclude part-time and domestic recipients, retain mandatory levy liability without registration, and require an election for the optional 5–9 class. HRD correction: declare employer scope, registration class, Form 2 count and optional threshold-crossing year; retain compulsory and optional high rates after headcount falls, including listed Part II NGOs.

limits.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(7): no more than twelve hours of work in any one day; s.60A(9) "hours of work" is the time the employee is at the employer’s disposal, so the twelve are worked hours, breaks excluded.
Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(b)
Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(c)
Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(d): not more than 45 hours of work in one week; s.60A(3) pays the hours beyond at one and a half times the hourly rate

Employment (Limitation of Overtime Work) Regulations 1980 reg. 2 sets 104 overtime hours in any one month for Employment Act 1955 s.60A(4)(a). The first proviso to s.60A(4)(a) excludes all work on a statutory rest day, a gazetted public holiday referred to in s.60D(1), or its paid substitute under s.60D. Ordinary-day and off-day overtime count; excluded days do not consume this cap. Separate daily limits and payment entitlements still apply.

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2 and 3, as substituted by the Employment (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2022 [P.U. (A) 262], in operation 1 January 2023 — the ladder in ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) and 60D(4) does not apply to a person whose wages exceed RM4,000 a month, save for the para 2 categories, which are covered irrespective of wages; para 2(4) vessel work is outside Part XII altogether; "wages" is the s.2 definition less commissions, subsistence allowance and overtime payment. The rest break is s.60A(1)(a): an employee shall not be required to work more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; proviso (i) a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours, proviso (ii) work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours inclusive of not less than forty-five minutes in the aggregate for a meal. The weekly rest day is s.59(1): every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as determined from time to time by the employer, and where more than one is allowed the LAST is the rest day for the purposes of Part XII; s.59(1A) treats any continuous period of not less than thirty hours as a rest day for shift work. holiday_rest_precedence is SUBSTITUTE on the s.60D(1) proviso: where a gazetted public holiday falls on a rest day, or on another public holiday, the working day next following is a paid holiday in substitution. APPLIED: (a) the s.60A(1)(b)-(d) statement of normal hours — not more than eight hours in one day ("normal_day"), a spread-over of not more than ten hours ("spread_day") and not more than forty-five hours in one week ("weekly_total") — enforced as schedule limits, while every BEYOND_NORMAL band below prices the overtime it derives; Applied 2026-09-18: s.60A(1)(b) the normal day is 8 hours, or up to 9 under the proviso where the contracted week is within 45 (`normal_hours`); s.60A(1)(d) 45 hours a week is a ceiling on normal hours, the hours beyond it overtime (`weekly_normal`, read by payroll), not a wall on the roster; s.60(3)(a) rest-day work of a daily- or hourly-rated employee pays one day’s wages up to half the normal hours and two days’ beyond (`person.terms.pay_frequency`); s.59(1A) the rest day does not run during maternity, sick or hospitalisation leave (`weekly_rest_rule.suspended_by_leave`); First Schedule para 2(5): a domestic employee is outside ss.60–60F and the overtime ladder (`employment.type != "DOMESTIC"`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the s.60A(7) daily limit `daily_total` is twelve WORKED hours (s.60A(9) defines hours of work as time at the employer’s disposal), not twelve clock hours less the break. Applied 2026-09-28: s.59(1) “where an employee is allowed more than one rest day in a week the last of such rest days shall be the rest day for the purposes of this Part” (`last_rest_day_only`) — an earlier REST-coded day of the same week is not the Part XII rest day, so s.60(3) does not price it: it prices as an off day, every hour beyond its (nil) normal hours at s.60A(3)(a) 1.5×. s.2 defines a week as “a continuous period of seven days” without fixing its start; the week is taken Monday–Sunday, as every weekly measure here is.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 2: a domestic employee is outside the Order. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1) and 5(1) print a daily rate by the number of working days in a week — RM65.38 (six), RM78.46 (five), RM98.08 (four) — and RM8.72 an hour. The run compares a daily contract as the month it makes (the rate × the 26-day divisor), so `scale` restates the printed daily rate as that month over the printed monthly RM1,700; `hourly_by_region` holds an hourly rate to RM8.72 directly (the three figures are one table of the Order and move together); a monthly contract is the monthly RM1,700 (scale 1). Para 2 excludes only a domestic servant; the INTERN exclusion rests on an intern on industrial training not being employed under a contract of service.

encashment.authority: Employment Act 1955 ss.2, 60E(3A), 60I(1A)-(1B): monthly wages / 26; weekly basic / 6. Contract allowances are monthly amounts, so qualifying normal-hours allowances add their monthly amount / 26. Excluded payments do not enter the rate.; s.60I(1C) for daily/hourly rates (preceding wage period)

ordinary_rate_reference.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60I(1C): total wages in the preceding wage period over the days actually worked

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.24(8): the total deducted under s.24 in a month may not exceed 50% of the wages earned in that month — s.24(2)(d) deductions authorized by another written law (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, MTD) are deductions under the section, and s.24(2)(c)/(4)(b) advance and loan recoveries count; s.24(9)(b) excludes from the limit only “deductions from the final payment of the wages of an employee for any amount due to the employer and remaining unpaid by the employee on the termination of the employee’s contract of service” — the loan and advance recoveries; the statutory and other deductions on the final payslip stay within the half (round 5, Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023). Applied: s.24(9)(a) exempts deductions FROM the notice indemnity payable BY the employer TO the employee (NOTICE_IN_LIEU), up to that payment; it does not generally exempt an indemnity owed by the employee. NOTICE_INDEMNITY is lawful under s.24(2)(b) and outside the half only on final pay under s.24(9)(b); s.24(9)(c) permits up to a further 25% solely for APPROVED_HOUSING_LOAN with the Director General's written permission recorded in approval_reference. The extra room never increases ordinary deductions. EA s.2 wage exclusions are classified by basis_exempt_codes; customer-specific codes must be classified in the sealed settings. Settled 2026-09-23 (round 4) from the Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023: s.24(1) “No deductions shall be made by an employer from the wages of an employee otherwise than in accordance with this Act”; s.24(2) “It shall be lawful for an employer to make the following deductions: … (d) deductions authorized by any other written law”; s.24(8) “The total of any amounts deducted under this section from the wages of an employee in respect of any one month shall not exceed fifty per centum of the wages earned by that employee in that month.” A statutory deduction (EPF employee share, SOCSO, EIS, MTD/PCB) is lawful only through s.24(2)(d) — s.24(1) admits no other route — so it is deducted under this section and counts toward the half; s.24(9) exempts it nowhere. The statutory charges are never shortened: they take their room first and only the counted recoveries are dropped.

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.21(2): an employee who terminates without notice under s.13(1)-(2) or s.14(3) is paid not later than the third day after the termination

Employment Act 1955 s.20 (a contract ending under s.11(1) or by notice under s.12, from either party) and s.21(1) (the employer terminating without notice): not later than the day the contract terminates
